blocks.x: ‘The Last of Us’ Offshoot Officially Killed Off by Sony

The Last of Us Part II was initially supposed to continue the original game’s popular Factions multiplayer mode, but Naughty Dog ultimately separated that experience from the sequel before transforming it into a far more ambitious standalone project. That game was officially canceled in 2023, leaving fans without a new multiplayer experience and Naughty Dog free to continue developing the single-player games for which the studio is best known.

A team of modders eventually decided to build the missing multiplayer mode themselves, complete with custom maps, perks, leaderboards, matchmaking, and support for 4v4 matches. After months of development and 25 minutes of gameplay footage, the unofficial project was finally expected to launch for The Last of Us Part II Remastered on PC this month, but its creators have now confirmed it will never be released.

Modder Speclizer announced that the planned Last of Us Part II multiplayer mod has been canceled after receiving a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting that it not be released. “Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day,” Speclizer wrote, thanking fans for supporting the project and revealing plans to move on to an original game. The project had reportedly been in development since January and attempted to create the multiplayer component that never accompanied The Last of Us Part II. Footage released earlier this year showed players competing across environments from the sequel while using many of its existing combat and stealth mechanics against one another.
